summary: The school district emphasizes the critical role of E-Rate in providing reliable broadband infrastructure for modern public education, citing the costs and benefits of preserving the program. The school district opposes proposals to sunset or eliminate E-Rate, emphasizing its role in providing connectivity for modern education and the need to preserve it for students' success.

claims.argument: The proposal to sunset E-Rate would eliminate essential federal funding for broadband infrastructure, increasing the burden on state and local budgets.
claims.evidence_quote: Mount Prospect School Dist 57 has received $259,430 in committed federal E-Rate support over funding years 2021–2025 — an average of roughly $51,886 a year toward the connections our students depend on.

claims.requested_action: Reject proposal to sunset or eliminate E-Rate program
claims.argument: E-Rate has enabled schools to provide connectivity necessary for modern education
claims.evidence_quote: E-Rate has enabled schools (public and private) and libraries to build and maintain the connectivity necessary for students and patrons to participate fully in modern education. As our nation seeks to prepare students for college, careers, and an increasingly technology-driven economy, now is not the time to undermine the very program and related infrastructure that makes those opportunities possible.
